reviews.title: Completely unusable
reviews.text: Crashes on launch. Has been broken for months. I reached out to them months ago but they never fixed it. Canceling my subscription

reviews.title: Fraud
reviews.text: I originally signed up for this $50 app and then they went to a subscription canceling out my initial purchase purchase.  Terrible

reviews.title: Paid for lifetime access, can no longer access.
reviews.text: I paid a (large) flat fee for this app back in the day. Then they switched to a subscription model and I lost my access. Super lame and disingenuous. Get Merlin instead.

reviews.title: No longer opens
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for 5 years. Now it asks to restore purchase but even after it says it has restored previous purchase it still won’t open. I’ve contacted customer support but have not gotten any response.

reviews.title: Cry foul
reviews.text:
A few years ago I purchased the lifetime version of the iBird Pro app. Loved the app. Then low and behold one day opened the app and it tells me I need a subscription.  Contacted the developer and the response was “we have gone to a different model now that requires a monthly or yearly subscription.” So I have to pay twice? 
Is this legal? Needless to say I deleted the app.  Now I see iBird is offering a lifetime subscription again. Probably won’t purchase due to the past experience.  My opinion is they played dirty pool.

reviews.title: Version 13.5.9 not working
reviews.text: App has always been great. However, the new version no longer works on my iPad Pro, or iPhone 12. The app opens normally, select a bird, it pulls up and everything freezes. Nothing is able to be selected, and you can’t even close it without closing the whole window. Sent in an email, but no response. It was a five star app for me before, but not now. I have to rate it one star now, because it does not work at all.

reviews.title: Subscription model ruined it
reviews.text: The app use to work great. I only used it a couple of times in the spring and fall to identify some birds now they want 10 bucks a month or some such thing for the same service not worth it in my book app has been deleted and never be used again.

reviews.title: “LIFETIME” PURCHASE IS A LIE
reviews.text:
I purchased this app 15 years ago. The developer now says I can get a “free 1 year subscription.”

I have sent 6 emails over the past month requesting the free offer code that the developer claims to offer.

I have heard nothing from the developer.

I say this free code claim is a lie that is told to make the developer seem like a reasonable person.

Shame on you!

__________

Previous UPDATE
Now I have sent 5 emails to IBird support and have gotten no reply regarding their claim that they will free 1 year subscriptions to previous purchasers of their app.
Either they are liars, they have a horrific support team or both. 

Previous review:
I PURCHASED iBird over 15 years ago, however a few weeks ago while banding birds, without warning the app said I need to subscribe to it to continue using iBird. Very inconvenient and irritating since I was without internet access to try to figure out what was going on. Legal? Probably. Sleazy? Definitely. They are still offering a Lifetime subscription. “Lifetime” according to these developers means “until we change our minds!” A less morally questionable option would be to offer Legacy access for previous purchasers of iBird that lets those users to continue to use the app without upgrades. Other apps have done this when they have moved to subscriptions. The developer states that users who purchased the app can get a free year subscription - just send an email to support. reviews.title: So frustrating! Unethical!
reviews.text: I am a professional guide and have been using this app regularly for almost 12 years. Two weeks ago, right before leaving for a guiding trip in Greenland, I made the mistake of updating the app. Got the “No Subscription Found" message and assumed there was just a glitch. Emailed support many times and have received no response. I finally got good enough internet today to search for this issue and was surprised to see that the app is now subscription based. I’m so disappointed… no notice and no support. I will be looking for a different birding app.

reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text: I purchased this app—it appears twice now, and now more features get taken away until it won’t work without a subscription. There are other apps out there that are better in price and performance.

reviews.title: Can’t restore my annual subscription!
reviews.text: Don’t subscribe! It asks you to restore your subscription every time and to no avail! Customer support is non existent. The send button is grayed out. Something is off about this!

reviews.title: Impossible to restore
reviews.text: I’m another one of the unhappy purchasers of iBird. I paid for the app years ago and then opened it one day to find my access had been revoked. I tried several times over several weeks to restore it and finally gave up. A couple of years later I am trying again and it’s impossible to get access still. Go check out the Audubon app which is awesome and adding new features regularly — and it will always be free and available.

reviews.title: Subscription
reviews.text: Stay away from this app. You will get screwed. Downloaded the app “for life version” and they cut off access and now require subscriptions. Use Sibley  or Merlin. Capitalism without clear and easy to understand policies is just theft. Stay away!

reviews.title: Paid to subscription
reviews.text: Went from a paid app to a subscription based model that made the app unusable without subscribing. Would never buy from them again.

reviews.title: Failure to address issue
reviews.text: I had a subscription to iBird Pro when it was first released about a decade ago. It was quite expensive by the standards of the time and then just disappeared unsupported and with it my money. I rediscovered that the app returned and I’ve tried to restore my subscription. I have sent numerous requests over a period of 5 weeks and although they have been noted, there is no response as to a resolution. I have been totally ignored since.

reviews.title: Still waiting
reviews.text: It’s been over 6 months and they still won’t tell me when or if they are going to give me my pictures back

reviews.title: Unethical company
reviews.text:
The app is great however the developer/company does not honor their agreements. Way back in the day I paid for lifetime access membership to the app and now I’ve been kicked out of my subscription. Their solution is to offer me a free 1 year subscription?!  Get lost you’re behaving badly, I’ll go find a different app that doesn’t screw people over. 

Great you want to switch to subscription model but how about you be loyal to the customers who built your base. I don’t want an apology and free 1 year. I want what I paid for. LIFETIME ACCESS

reviews.title: Here’s your star
reviews.text:
Take your one star and your “free” 1 year subscription and shove it up your cloaca. 
Sincerely, a previous “lifetime” owner. 
p.s. you can save your AI generated response- it makes your company look even worse and screws the environment.

reviews.title: Rip off
reviews.text:
Before you pay for this app, I would recommend the Merlin app or Audubon app.  Both are free and the developers don’t rip off long time users.  
I purchased iBird Pro, iBird Ultimate, iBird Journal and iBird Photo Sleuth and loved them all…up until the developer switched to a subscription model.  To rub further salt in the wound, they now have a “Lifetime Subscription” option.  I had a lifetime purchase and spent more than the $59.99 they are now asking for all the apps I purchased over the years. Why not give purchasers of your apps the Lifetime subscription instead of trying to placate them with a one year slap in the face…just another money grab.
Oh, and you can also forget trying to contact the developers, they only respond to people who stroke their egos.

reviews.title: Good App, Bad Business
reviews.text: This is a great app and have used it for years. I have several bird apps on my phone but this is the one I always go to, or at least it was. So why the 1-star rating. Waite Group may be a great app developer but they are also a business, and, as a business, they suck. I had a lot of trouble converting to the subscription when they started charging a monthly fee. I wanted to pay them, but they couldn’t make it possible. E-mails went unanswered. Recently I had trouble updating to the latest version. They sent a fix. Today I was out in the field and when I tried to access the app I got a message saying the beta version had expired. No warning. I didn’t even know I had a beta. That was their fix. I get home to WiFi and still no access. I’m done with them.

reviews.title: No to subscription
reviews.text: After paying $14.99 for your app, it is wrong to refuse access unless I subscribe. It’s like buying a book and then taking it away unless I rent it from you every month. I have no desire for a free year either. Unethical behavior.

reviews.title: Unethical change!
reviews.text: Without warning, iBird Pro changed to a subscription model. They should have at least given those of us who purchased the app years ago a heads up that updating the app would render it useless unless we agreed to a monthly fee. I’d have been happy keeping the old “out of date” app that I paid for. There are plenty of other excellent birding apps to choose from. I do not recommend iBird Pro. Shifting from a purchase to a subscription is unethical for those of us who already paid for the app!
